title: Liability Impact Estimator and Legal Routing Heuristics for Pricing Experiments
creator: Asha Raman
description: Build an automated estimator that quantifies the incremental commercial risk (liability/indemnity exposure and likely concession bands) introduced by MSA/DPA redlines surfaced during sales pricing experiments, and wire that estimator into a deterministic routing heuristic that decides whether a legal review is required and which lane (Fast Review / Full Legal / Escalation) to send the request to. The goal is to reduce manual triage time for high-volume pricing tests and ensure pricing experiments yield correct unit economics while keeping legal review load predictable.
acceptance_criteria: Estimator outputs a normalized liability delta score (0-100) for a redline payload including indemnity, cap, and escrow clauses and maps to a recommended legal lane
Routing heuristic uses estimator score + customer tier + revenue estimate to choose one of: auto-approve, fast-review, full-legal-review, escalate-to-legal-lead
Sales UI shows the liability delta, recommended lane, and top 3 clause contributors, with link to suggested mitigations (e.g., reduce cap, propose alternative language)
Reduce manual legal triage time for pricing experiments by >= 40% in initial pilot (measure via ticket time-to-resolution and hand-offs)
End-to-end flow includes audit log entry and links to generated evidence bundle for security/finance review
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Rules-driven estimator based on clause fingerprinting and weighted heuristics derived from historical redlines (weighting for indemnity, cap size, carve-outs)
Phase 2: ML scoring model using historical legal decisions and outcomes (requires dataset and legal approval)
Store provenance for every score: clause fingerprints, inputs (customer tier, ARR), and model version or ruleset id
Integration points: Sales CRM (pre-fill ARR/tier), Contract intake API, Legal queueing service (ENG-queue), Console UI flagging
Expose a sandbox mode for pricing experiments to simulate expected legal load before running large-scale experiments
